methodology: own Go loadgen (cmd/loadgen), 30s per scenario unless noted, same machine, backends over their own local Postgres (Go: pilot pg18 @4632 single binary; Node: reference stack @5432 api+worker+redis). start/diamond latency = start→terminal via /v1/status polling (20ms). No pass/fail threshold — learning numbers.

diamond5vu_15s.note: 2 runs POLL-TIMED-OUT at 90s — stuck diamonds (~0.45%); an earlier unbounded 10vu attempt hung indefinitely on the same shape

findings: Go wins clearly at low-contention: start@10vu 4.1x runs/s at 5.7x lower p50; list 2.6x RPS at 2.3x lower p50; diamond@10vu 4.6x runs/s vs Node's bounded 5vu sample.

Go start@50vu degrades hard at worker concurrency 8 (p99 19.9s); raising concurrency to 32 fixes the tail (p99 2.3s) but throughput stays ~49/s and diamond@c32 COLLAPSES 8x — prime suspect: the db pool hardcoded at MaxConns 10 starves 32 workers + API pollers. Follow-up: configurable pool size, separate API/worker pools, retest.
Node degrades gracefully at 50vu (53/s, p99 1.9s) — BullMQ's async job model parallelizes beyond OS threads; the Go pool must scale with its connection budget to match.

Node stuck-diamond reproduction: 2/445 diamonds never completed (join never fired). The Go engine completed 4100/4100. Candidate confirmation of the readiness-scan ordering hazard already flagged upstream.
Footprint: Go 21.9MB idle single process (29.9MB under load) vs Node ~101MB idle across api+worker plus Redis.

go_after_t019.config: c=32, API pool 10, worker pool 34 (separated), loadgen keep-alive fixed
notes: start@50vu: 49.3→274.6 runs/s (5.6x) and p99 19.9s→337ms (59x) — the pool separation WAS the cliff.
list@50vu: 2800→6220 RPS with p50 17.9→6.6ms — the dedicated API pool doubled reads.

diamond@10vu with c=32 lands at 90/s vs 136/s at c=8: per-run advisory-lock contention grows with worker count over few runs; still 3x Node. Concurrency should scale with concurrent RUNS, not just nodes.

First retest showed 7628 loadgen-side errors at 500 runs/s: Go's default Transport MaxIdleConnsPerHost=2 caused ephemeral-port churn — a LOADGEN artifact (backend clean: 11966/11966 runs succeeded); fixed with keep-alive 512.
